name: InterContinental - ANA Tokyo
positioning: ANA InterContinental Tokyo: a central Tokyo hotel in the Ark Hills complex in Akasaka, on the Roppongi side, with Kintsugi-inspired rooms and a two-floor Club lounge
best_for: Travelers who want a central Tokyo base near embassies, government offices and Roppongi
Families wanting a suite that sleeps four

facts.text: The hotel is in central Tokyo, close to government offices, embassies and major companies.
The hotel is located in the Ark Hills complex, which includes a classic concert hall.
The address is technically Akasaka, but on the Roppongi side, a short walk to Roppongi's restaurants and bars.
Suntory Hall is two minutes from the hotel.
Guest rooms offer views of Tokyo Tower, the Imperial Palace Gardens or Roppongi.
Rooms have designs inspired by the Japanese art of Kintsugi.
The lobby has soaring double-height ceilings gridded with geometric lights, warm wood paneling and a glowing staircase.
The Club InterContinental Lounge spans the 35th and 36th floors and is exclusively for guests in Club rooms and suites.
The hotel's spa, THANN Sanctuary Spa Akasaka, is a tranquil pocket of the property.
Unkai Japanese Restaurant overlooks a traditional garden and pond and offers private tatami dining rooms for traditional cuisine such as kaiseki.
MIXX Bar and Lounge on the 36th floor overlooks the Tokyo metropolis.
The hotel took the InterContinental name in 2007 after ANA's hotel business merged with IHG.

highlights.text: The outdoor pool is on the fourth floor, which Conde Nast Traveler calls rare for central Tokyo.
Rooms lean into subdued Japanese modernism with origami-inspired geometric patterns.
The two-floor Club InterContinental Lounge sits high above the city on the 35th and 36th floors.
Family suites sleep four with the sofa bed and can be booked without lounge access.
A bio-treatment system recycles kitchen wastewater, rainwater and pool water for flushing toilets.

considerations.text: The outdoor pool is seasonal and opens in the summer.
The sauna is in the men's changing room only.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing that may not suit budget-conscious travelers.
